paragraphs: Children in care in Bournemouth are looked after by BCP Council, the council for Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole, and by the independent agencies shown above. The council's fostering service is run from the Civic Centre in Bournemouth and works across the whole BCP area, recruiting carers for children and young people from birth to 18.

BCP Council says it needs more foster carers and that it recruits only people who live locally, so that children can stay near their schools, friends and families. When the council set out its fostering drive in May 2024 it said it wanted another 30 foster families, and it asked in particular for more applications from single people, same-sex couples, disabled people and people from diverse ethnic communities. In February 2026 it backed What I Need Most, a campaign from the regional Fostering South West partnership, and said that when no local home is available a child can end up placed 20 miles or more away.

Fostering with the council can mean full-time care, shared care, supported lodgings or short breaks. Carers get tailored training, ongoing guidance, financial support and access to a support network. Since December 2024 the council has also run the Mockingbird model, in which a group of foster families is linked to an experienced hub home carer for advice, sleepovers where appropriate and shared activities, an approach designed to make placements more stable.

The council says what matters is being able to give a child a safe, stable home where they feel part of the family, whether you are married or single. Speak to BCP Fostering and to two or three of the agencies above, and compare training, support and payments before you choose. Poole has its own page on this site.
